deep.reconstruction:
The verso is essentially blank. The only writing is a short column of small numbers near the right margin and two marks at the bottom corner. All of it is written upside down relative to the scan, so the sheet was turned when it was used as scrap. Reading it right way up, there are three column additions with two-decimal numbers and a decimal comma:
(1) 6,39 + 2,52 + 2,38 = 11,29. Check: 6.39 + 2.52 = 8.91; 8.91 + 2.38 = 11.29.
(2) 5,18 + 1,26 = 6,44.
(3) 16,79 + 1,26 = 18,05.
The same summand 1,26 appears in (2) and (3). That suggests a fixed additive charge or correction added to two different base amounts, perhaps a fee, postage or some measured quantity, but nothing on the page settles what. The decimal parts (39, 52, 38) exceed 30 and 60, so these are not Thaler/Silbergroschen or Gulden/Kreuzer sums; they are decimal quantities.
The two marks at the bottom, transcribed '512.' and '513.', are most likely archival foliation numbers, one superseded by the other, rather than mathematics. They might conceivably be read as '5/12' and '5/13'.
No mathematical derivation is present. According to the next-page notes, the bundle contains material on Riemann's 1851 doctoral disputation and dissertation, and this sheet seems to be a wrapper or back leaf carrying incidental arithmetic.

results.what: Elementary decimal additions (scrap bookkeeping or measurement arithmetic)

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds only three trivial, correct additions of decimal numbers written as marginal scrap, plus archival numbering. There is no mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: All the writing is upside down relative to the scan; the sheet was rotated 180 degrees when written on.
The third block's first summand could be read as 16,78 in the image, but only 16,79 is consistent with the sum 18,05, so 16,79 is retained.
The second block's first number may carry a faint leading stroke (it looks like '25,18' in the image), but the sum 6,44 requires 5,18.
'512.' and '513.' at the bottom are probably archival folio numbers (possibly read as '5/12', '5/13'), not part of the computation.
